name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: local-buffer type-erased Function
listed_description: Book's own generic type-erased callable wrapper with a template-sized inline buffer, a never-null executor pointer and the callable pointer passed as the last argument so calls compile to a tail jump; code is in the Chapter07 folder of the companion repository.
claim_text: Book reports about 0.884 ns per call for its Function against 1.33 ns for std::function; a direct lambda call takes 0.219 ns.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, one lambda capturing a value, four int arguments, call result kept alive with DoNotOptimize; example build line uses -g -O3 --std=c++20 with g++-11 or clang++; CPU not stated; first-party numbers by the book author.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 6 Type Erasure, sections Efficient type erasure and Performance of type erasure

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: local-buffer type-erased smart pointer
listed_description: Book's own type-erased owning pointer that stores its deleter in an inline buffer (static function pointer or hand-built vtable variants) so no second allocation is needed; Chapter07 folder of the companion repository.
claim_text: Construct plus destroy of one int: about 9.58 ns static-function variant and 10.4 ns vtable variant, against 22.9 ns for std::shared_ptr with custom deleter and 17.5 ns for make_shared.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, new int(0) allocated in a separate translation unit, raw pointer 8.72 ns and std::unique_ptr 8.82 ns as floor; -g -O3 --std=c++20, whole-program optimization off; CPU not stated; first-party. Shared pointer also does reference counting, so the comparison is not feature-equal.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 6 Type Erasure, section Performance of type erasure (The overhead of type erasure)

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: CRTP static polymorphism
listed_description: Curiously Recurring Template Pattern used as compile-time replacement for virtual function dispatch; Chapter08 folder of the companion repository.
claim_text: Per-call time for 32 repeated calls: virtual call 9.04 ns against 1.55 ns for CRTP call and 1.60 ns for a plain non-virtual call.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, trivial member function incrementing a counter, base-class pointer, 32 calls per iteration; compiler, flags and CPU not stated; first-party. Virtual dispatch gives extra runtime flexibility, so the comparison is not feature-equal.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 8 The Curiously Recurring Template Pattern, sections What is wrong with a virtual function and Introducing CRTP

name: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++ 2nd ed: local buffer optimization small_string
listed_description: Book's small-string class that keeps short text inside the object instead of a heap block, shown against a naive strdup-based string; Chapter10 folder of the companion repository.
claim_text: Create short string: 18.7 ns against 835 ns for 32 creations; copy 53.5 ns against 786 ns; comparing 4M strings about 2x faster.
book_benchmark: Google Benchmark, 13-character string, 32 repetitions per iteration, 1 to 4 threads, compare over 4194304 strings (15.06 ms against 30.23 ms); compiler, flags and CPU not stated; baseline is the book's own naive heap-allocating simple_string, not std::string; first-party.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 10 Local Buffer Optimization, section Effect of local buffer optimization

name: zoo (thecppzoo)
listed_description: Header-only C++17 library by Eduardo Madrid; the book says its efficient type-erased Function was inspired by Madrid's and Arthur O'Dwyer's work. Book does not name the repository; match is a guess from the author's name.
listed_license: MIT (per GitHub page, not stated in book)
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 6 Type Erasure, section Efficient type erasure
